clue.text: Leather horse's head found in compound

indicators.note: found in says the horse's head letter sits within the compound word

parts.note: an oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen

indicators.note: the head of the word horse is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A leather-worker's horse's head turns up in an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like an enclosure for a horse, but it is a chemical compound, OXIDE, with H put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned hide from a bullock is a kind of leather.

clue.text: Old clergyman upset _ church, including leaders of Mothers' Union, excessively

indicators.note: including has the turned title and church take in the leaders
upset in a down clue turns the clergyman's title upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

indicators.note: leaders are the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An old vicar is upset by the Mothers' Union taking over his church far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REV to VER; 'including' puts MU between VER and CH. The gap in the clue is a lost word, probably 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overmuch is an adverb meaning too much, to excess.

clue.text: Cowl on chimney is rowdy

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the cowl above the chimney

parts.note: a cowl is a hood
lum is a Scottish and northern word for chimney

explanation.surface: A cowl on a chimney is noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy is a noisy, violent hooligan, as is a gangster thug.

clue.text: Withdraw from combat and slip out-of gear

definitions.meaning: to pull troops back and break off fighting
to release a mechanism so its parts no longer mesh

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to release or detach: an army from battle, a clutch from a gearbox.

clue.text: Well-heeled worker installed fine sort of pipe

indicators.note: the worker has the other pieces installed inside him, so they go within his letters

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword favourite for a worker
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a flue is a pipe or duct carrying smoke

explanation.surface: A prosperous householder has a workman fit a good chimney pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled is an idiom for wealthy or prosperous.

clue.text: At liberty to introduce an award, say, in commercial competition

parts.note: free means at liberty
to enter is to put in or introduce

indicators.note: say signals the word is matched by its sound only

parts.note: a prize is an award

explanation.surface: Freedom to bring in a prize in the world of business rivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: The economic system of private business competing with little state control.

clue.text: Security device used in cathedral at Chichester

indicators.note: used in says the answer sits within the run of letters cathedral at Chichester

explanation.surface: A security device fitted in Chichester's cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a fastening bar for a door or gate.

clue.text: Beginnings of relief raised to support former soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath the former soldiers

parts.note: ex means former
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: raised in a down clue has the word for relief read upwards

parts.note: aid is relief or help

explanation.surface: The start of a relief operation raised to help ex-servicemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AID to DIA, which sits below EX + OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Exordia are introductions to speeches or treatises, their opening parts.

clue.text: Old Greek scholar residing in the north

indicators.note: the scholar resides inside the other letters

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A classical scholar living up north.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Thebes, the ancient city-state of Boeotia, was an ancient Hellene.

clue.text: Liberal president noted head's similar disposition

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower
minded means heeded or noted
a ness is a headland or head

explanation.surface: A Liberal president noticed his leader shared his outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of one mind with others means sharing the same outlook or temperament.

clue.text: See Cassio dancing to this tune

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of the two words moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch Shakespeare's Cassio dance to a melody.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassio is Othello's lieutenant; the anagram of SEE CASSIO gives the Scottish country-dance tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecossaise is a lively Scottish-style dance and the music written for it.

clue.text: Square house with quarters for the people yonder

parts.note: a T-square gives T for square
S and E are two compass quarters, south and east

explanation.surface: A square house with living quarters for distant folk.
explanation.definitionFit: The demonstrative pronoun for persons over there, as in 'those yonder'.

clue.text: English archbishop in Maine causing confusion

indicators.note: in places the English archbishop inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine
Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury 1928-42

explanation.surface: An English churchman in Maine stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: LANG is Cosmo Gordon Lang, Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1930s; 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a mixture or jumble, hence a state of confusion.

clue.text: Spiny little animal can hide in jungle

indicators.note: a jungle is a tangled mess, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A small prickly creature is able to conceal itself in the jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia is a small egg-laying mammal covered in spines.

clue.text: Order last two characters to leave for a short break

indicators.note: the final pair of letters of the word for order are told to go away

parts.note: a command is an order

explanation.surface: Two characters are told to go off for a quick rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In punctuation this mark signals a brief pause in a sentence.

clue.text: This one man disrupted these games

indicators.note: disrupted means the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One player alone spoiled the competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isthmian Games were ancient Greek athletic festivals held at Corinth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isthmian Games were one of the four great Panhellenic athletic festivals.

clue.text: The physician can be healed!

definitions.note: a verb phrase, read as '(able to) be healed' to match the adjective

parts.note: a medic is a doctor or physician
able means can, having the capacity

explanation.surface: A doctor declares the patient curable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' gives ABLE, which also carries the definition's sense of being able to be healed.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicable means curable, capable of treatment.

clue.text: Perry encompassed Mark's overthrow, the old beast!

indicators.note: encompassed has the surname wrap round the other piece

parts.note: Perry Mason is the fictional lawyer, so Perry gives his surname

indicators.note: overthrow in a down clue tips the mark upside down so it reads upwards

parts.note: a dot is a mark

explanation.surface: Perry plotted Mark's downfall, the old brute!
explanation.walkthrough: Perry Mason is Erle Stanley Gardner's TV lawyer; 'overthrow' turns DOT to TOD, put in MASON.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon is an extinct elephant-like animal from prehistoric times.

clue.text: Malefactor's aim to disrupt proposal

definitions.note: read as 'malefactor is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the aim breaks into the proposal, sitting inside it

parts.note: an offer is a proposal
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A villain sets out to wreck a deal on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer or criminal.

clue.text: He ensures his footwear is fitting for the Arabs

definitions.text: He ensures his footwear is fitting for the Arabs

parts.words: He ensures his footwear is fitting for the Arabs
parts.note: the Arabs are horses, and 'his footwear' the shoes this tradesman nails on them

explanation.definitionFit: A farrier shoes horses, including the Arab breed.

clue.text: Had accident when carrying keys to Russian cottage

indicators.note: the jumbled letters carry the keys inside them
an accident leaves things in a mess, so the three letters are jumbled

parts.note: C and A are musical keys

explanation.surface: Someone crashed while bringing keys to a country house in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident' turns HAD into DHA; 'when carrying' puts AC inside it after the D. 'to' is a link leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or holiday villa.

clue.text: Fashion designing unacceptable in the parish priest's domain

indicators.note: in places the word for unacceptable inside the priest's domain

parts.note: a cure is a priest's charge, the cure of souls in a parish
out means not allowed or unacceptable

explanation.surface: Fashion is frowned on in the vicar's parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Couture is the business of designing and making fine fashionable clothes.

clue.text: Container for a type of food prepared in layers

definitions.text: Container for a type of food prepared in layers

parts.words: Container for a type of food prepared in layers
parts.note: the layers are hens, which produce the food; it is not a layered dish

explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holds a boiled egg, a food laid by hens.

clue.text: Gum's literary anthology?

definitions.meaning: the actress Judy ... was born Frances Gumm, so her stage name is Gum(m)'s
an old word for a collection of poems or prose pieces

explanation.walkthrough: Judy Garland, star of The Wizard of Oz, was born Frances Ethel Gumm; the clue may have printed Gumm's.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage surname adopted by the Gumm girl, and an old term for a poetry collection.

clue.text: A governor of the present era is further advanced

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor
AD, anno Domini, is the present era

explanation.surface: A governor of our time is more progressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front means having progressed further than others.

clue.text: Striker in court making a commotion, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound, not spelling

parts.note: a racket is a din or commotion

explanation.surface: A batsman in court makes a terrible din.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'court' is a tennis or squash court, and the striker the bat used there.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis or squash bat strikes the ball on a court.

clue.text: Feature to note in a deep ravine

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A feature is added to a note on a steep gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: Chine is a dialect word, chiefly on the Isle of Wight, for a deep narrow ravine.

clue.text: Tom Brown's friend compelled to describe a journey from Rugby to Cambridge

definitions.text: a journey from Rugby to Cambridge
definitions.note: a noun phrase describing travel in one direction; the answer is the adjective for it

parts.note: Harry East is Tom's friend in Tom Brown's Schooldays
bound means obliged or compelled

explanation.surface: A Rugby schoolboy is obliged to travel to university.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Brown's Schooldays is set at Rugby School; Cambridge lies east of the town of Rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling from Rugby to Cambridge one heads towards the rising sun.

clue.text: One's seen in procession in' the animal park

indicators.note: seen in places one's letters inside the procession

parts.note: a parade is a procession
one's is I'S, one being the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted marching in a parade through the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Persian for an enclosed park or garden where animals were kept.

clue.text: Change of direction at end of dangerous river

indicators.text: Change of direction at end of
indicators.note: the final compass-point letter, east, is swapped for another direction, north

parts.note: severe can mean grave or dangerous, as in a severe injury

explanation.surface: A sharp turn at the end of a hazardous river.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVERE ends in E (east); changing that direction to N (north) gives the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river in Britain, flowing from Wales to the Bristol Channel.
